newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent Group Three diesel surges higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent Group Three diesel surges higher.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot low sulphur diesel prices surged higher on Wednesday, fueled by a draw in distillate stocks and refiner buying, traders said.

Distillate stocks in PADD II, which covers the Chicago and Group Three markets, were drawn down 2.77 million barrels last week, due largely to an outage at BP's 155,000 barrel per day Toledo, Ohio refinery.

The draw and sightings of cooperative Farmland Industries Inc seeking spot diesel barrels pushed differentials higher on spot barrels in the Group Three market centered in Kansas City, Mo., traders said.
Group Three low sulphur diesel for late-October deliveries was talked 4.75/5.0 cents a gallon over NYMEX November heating oil, with high sulphur steady at 2.0 cents over.
Chicago low sulphur diesel firmed to even to 0.25 cent over the print, with high sulphur barrels modestly lower at 2.75 cents a gallon under the print.
Traders said late-season harvest demand was continuing to drive strength in diesel prices.
Group Three October unleaded eased to even to 0.25 cent a gallon over NYMEX November unleaded, with premium steady at 3.0 cents higher.
Chicago unleaded for late-October deliveries was talked 0.50/0.75 cents a gallon over the print and premium was 3.0 cents higher, unchanged on the day.
